findings.detail: Convention check #8 (hard fail: no imports from @nestfolio/integration-testing) is violated — two E2E test bodies import EventBusTrap from the integration-testing harness, and two shared helpers do as well.

findings.detail: src/index.ts barrel (config check #5) omits three helpers that are imported across many test files via relative paths: event-subject-trap (armEventSubjectTrap), contract-assert (expectContractMatch), and graphql-types (response types). freshTenant/waitForGraphQL/poll/bffClient/fixtures/alpacaPaperReset/AgentTraceTrap are exported, so the barrel is inconsistent about which helpers are the public surface.
findings.evidence: src/index.ts exports 8 helper modules but not event-subject-trap/contract-assert/graphql-types; e.g. src/account/go-live-switch.e2e.test.ts:11 `import { armEventSubjectTrap } from '../helpers/event-subject-trap'`, src/advisory/advisory-contract-emission.e2e.test.ts:113 `import { expectContractMatch } from '../helpers/contract-assert'`, src/funding/fund-account.e2e.test.ts:13 `import type { RecentActivityResponse } from '../helpers/graphql-types'`

findings.detail: Convention check #5 requires DDB reads in test bodies to carry a comment explaining why GraphQL is insufficient. Several assertion-path DDB reads lack that justification comment. The compliance-ctrl polls (no BFF, so GraphQL genuinely unavailable) are justified in principle but never state it; go-live-switch reads investor-bff's own InvestorProfile row directly (a table that is a BFF read model reachable via GraphQL) with no justification.
findings.evidence: src/account/go-live-switch.e2e.test.ts:57 GetCommand on investor-bff InvestorProfile (BFF read model); src/advisory/operating-mode-authority.e2e.test.ts:60/79 and src/profile/update-operating-mode.e2e.test.ts:54/78 (compliance-ctrl reads, comment only says 'Set up DDB client for compliance-ctrl reads'); src/advisory/reconciliation-correction.e2e.test.ts:64/93

findings.detail: Contract `SimDepositInitiatedSubjectSchema` uses a forbidden `Subject` suffix (typed-subject convention 4). It should be named after the clean domain/event concept (e.g. `SimDepositInitiatedSchema`). Not present in runtime/content/exclusions/typed-subject-exclusions.json, so it is an unjustified violation flagged by `event-processor:typed-subject-drift`.
findings.evidence: services/execution/broker-ctrl/src/domain/contracts.ts:76 — `node tools/check-typed-subjects.mjs` → [subject-suffix]

findings.detail: Contract `SimWithdrawalRequestedSubjectSchema` uses a forbidden `Subject` suffix (typed-subject convention 4).
